K8Secret 0.6.14 — clusters whose certificates outlive Apple's rules.

This is the fix for 'a TLS error caused the secure connection to fail' on a cluster that kubectl connects to perfectly well.

macOS applies Apple's requirements for public website certificates to every connection an app makes, and one of them is that a server certificate may not be valid for more than 398 days. Kubernetes clusters routinely issue themselves certificates that last two years — Azure's AKS gives its API server 731 days — so macOS refused them, after K8Secret had already checked the certificate against the certificate authority in your own kubeconfig and found it good. The connection died before your client certificate was ever asked for, which is why the error blamed TLS and mentioned nothing you could act on. Newer versions of macOS enforce this where older ones did not, which is why the same kubeconfig worked on one Mac and not another.

K8Secret now does this verification itself rather than deferring to rules written for public websites. Your cluster's certificate is still checked, and checked more strictly than before: against the certificate authority in your kubeconfig and nothing else, with the hostname verified, and with a refusal rather than a fallback if that authority cannot be read. Skipping verification remains something only you can turn on, in your own kubeconfig.

Found by a user who ran the diagnostics on the machine where it failed, across seven releases. Thank you.
